title: PN Synthetic X-ray Event Distribution (KDE)

citation.text: ESPAI PN Synthetic X-ray Event Distribution (KDE) (Version 1.0). Generated using Kernel Density Estimation.

abstract: This dataset contains 1,981,558 synthetic X-ray photon events generated using a Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) approach. The data simulates the distribution of events on an X-ray detector (XMM-Newton EPIC-pn), characterized by spatial coordinates and energy channels. Each row represents a single photon event with detector coordinates (DETX, DETY) and Pulse Invariant (PI) energy values. This distribution is suitable for background modeling, instrument simulation, or testing machine learning algorithms in high-energy astrophysics.
purpose: Generate realistic synthetic X-ray detector events for training machine learning models, background subtraction, or instrument response simulation.

provenance.sources: Generated via Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) trained on observational data (implied PN event lists).
provenance.processing: 1) KDE model training on source distribution, 2) Resampling/Generation of synthetic events.
provenance.derivations: Synthetic event list containing DETX, DETY, and PI columns.

structure.conventions: Columns: DETX (Detector X coordinate), DETY (Detector Y coordinate), PI (Pulse Invariant energy channel). DETX/DETY range: typical for EPIC-pn detector. PI range: ~300 to 12000.
structure.relationships: Single table containing photon events and data columns (DETX, DETY, PI).

quality.validation: Statistical distribution matches the source KDE model.
quality.usageGuidance: Suitable for statistical studies of detector distribution or ML training.

access.reuseGuidance: Suitable for academic research and machine learning applications
